title: SRE weekly ops spotlight — incident hypotheses & handoff notes
content:
Purpose:
This note is a short, pragmatic weekly snapshot focusing on two items: 1) a running incident hypothesis thread for the partial-throttle event on 2025-04-05 and 2) the on-call handoff checklist for the week of Apr 7–14. Goal is to capture open hypotheses, quick mitigations, and owners so the incoming on-call has a concise context.

Executive summary:
- Incident (2025-04-05 03:12–04:00 UTC): partial throttling observed across a subset of hosted inference pods serving the text-generation API. Impact: 2–7% increased tail latency for 95th/99th percentile, elevated error rate on small bursty requests for ~45 minutes. No customer-facing downtime, but noticeable SLO drift on model-route 'gptx-64k'.
- Current status: mitigations applied (circuit opened for failing backend, temporary route split to smaller model variant). Engineering follow-up in progress; next steps listed below.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 03:12 UTC: Pager alert — elevated 99p latency on model-route gptx-64k.
- 03:15 UTC: On-call routed traffic away from two pods with repeated socket timeouts.
- 03:22 UTC: Autoscaler triggered extra replicas; we saw partial recovery.
- 03:30 UTC: Fallback policy engaged — route split to gptx-16k for latency-sensitive requests.
- 03:58 UTC: Error rates returned to baseline; monitoring shows normalizing tail latencies.

Initial data & signals observed:
- Host-level: CPU on affected nodes spiked ~30% vs baseline; GPU util remained steady.
- Network: Increased retransmits on one AZ (us-west-2a) for approx 25 minutes.
- Runtime: KV cache pressure increased; cache miss ratio on affected pods rose from 0.12 to 0.46.
- Queueing: request queue length for the worker process spiked for short window (seen in per-pod histograms).

Working hypotheses (rank-ordered):
1) Network flakiness in us-west-2a caused transient packet loss leading to socket retries, which amplified request latency and increased KV-cache churn (most likely).
   Evidence: retransmits, AZ-local skew, matching timeline with queue spikes.
   Quick test: reproduce load against affected AZ with simulated packet loss.
2) Autoscaling race condition + bursty traffic pattern produced short-lived hot shards where prefix cache warmed slowly.
   Evidence: autoscaler activity observed and cache miss increase.
   Quick test: run synthetic burst test on staging with current autoscaler config and measure cache miss behavior.
3) Edge LB health-check configuration caused delayed failover on a subset of pods.
   Evidence: small number of pods reported socket timeouts while others healthy; need to validate health-check logs.

Immediate mitigations applied (done during incident):
- Route split to lower-capacity model variant for latency-sensitive routes (owner: Arjun P.).
- Marked two pods unhealthy and drained them to prevent noisy neighbors (owner: Ethan B.).
- Increased short-term autoscaler aggressiveness on the pool serving gptx-64k (ops flag change).

Open action items (owners and ETA):
- A1: Network postmortem request — collect packet-level logs from us-west-2a and open a cloud provider ticket if retransmit patterns persist. Owner: Sofia M. ETA: 2025-04-10.
- A2: Autoscaler stress test in staging to validate race condition hypothesis; run with synthetic bursts. Owner: Arjun P. ETA: 2025-04-14. Link: RDW-1243.
- A3: Runbook addendum — add explicit steps for 'route split' fallback with exact CLI commands and rollback steps. Owner: Maya C. ETA: 2025-04-12.
- A4: Observability tweak — add KV cache miss ratio alert (threshold TBD) and dashboard panel for per-AZ cache miss. Owner: Ethan B. ETA: 2025-04-11. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/467

SLO impact & math (quick):
- Affected route: gptx-64k latency SLO (p95 < 120ms, p99 < 400ms), monthly target 99.95 availability.
- Incident window ~0.8 hours; 99p breached for ~45 minutes for small subset of traffic (~3% of total). Estimated SLO burn for the week: ~0.004% (rough estimate). We'll calculate final numbers in postmortem.

Runbook notes & proposed changes:
- Observation: current runbook step 'drain unhealthy' is ambiguous about whether to adjust autoscaler -- add explicit 'pause autoscaler scale-in for 10m' guidance.
- Add a diagnosis checklist: (1) check per-AZ network retransmit graphs, (2) check KV cache miss ratio, (3) check per-node queue histograms.
- Low-friction fallback: we should document a one-command route-split hack that product/solutions can reuse during high-latency events.

Handoff checklist for incoming on-call (Apr 7 08:00 UTC -> Apr 14 08:00 UTC):
- Read this doc and the linked artifacts (RDW-1243).
- Primary outstanding tasks: A1, A2, A3, A4 (see owners/ETAs above). Be ready to escalate network evidence if retransmits persist.
- Observability pointers: dashboard 'SRE / gptx-64k / per-AZ' (pinned in SRE Grafana folder), alert 'gptx-64k 99p spike' (threshold currently 370ms).
- Contact list:
  - On-call escalation: Sofia Martinez (pager), Ethan Brooks (pager), Arjun Patel (slack).
  - Cloud provider account lead: Joanna Park (cloudops).

Meeting summary (standup 2025-04-07, 09:15 UTC):
- Quick sync with infra + serving runtime. Key points: autoscaler logs captured, but need more stress tests; engineering agreed to add the KV cache miss alert and draft runbook changes this week.
- Decision: do not change global SLO until postmortem analysis. Communicate to product if more than one SLO day burns.

Notes to self / informal TODOs:
- Check if the affected nodes are pinned to older NIC drivers — ask infra to surface kernel/driver versions.
- Add a short script to correlate per-pod queue histograms with packet retransmit spikes (low-effort, high-value).
- Slack thread: #sre-ops -> thread titled "Apr05 partial throttle: initial hypothesis" (link pinned in confluence page).

Unresolved questions:
- Is the retransmit spike caused by infra maintenance or backbone issues? (need cloud provider logs).
- Could a model-variant memory pressure cause the cache churn independently of network? (need memory/oom reports).

Appendix — quick links and debug commands (for incoming on-call):
- List pods with recent socket timeouts: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running | grep Timeout
- Drain a pod (safe): kubectl cordon/evict pattern (see runbook snippet).
- Toggle route-split (internal CLI): redwood route split --from gptx-64k --to gptx-16k --percent 20

If anything unexpected happens while I am away, tag me @maya in pager thread; I will monitor on-call rotations in parallel.

-- Maya C.
